steps: Raise your dominant hand, palm facing outward, fingers together.
Push it firmly forward toward the person or thing you want to stop.
Keep your expression serious to match a 'halt' command.
tip: “Stops” is signed with the base STOP sign.

steps: Curve your dominant hand into a loose C shape, as if holding a cup.
Lift the hand up to your mouth.
Tip your wrist toward your face, as though taking a drink from the cup.
tip: “Drinks” is signed with the base DRINK sign.

steps: Hold your dominant hand flat, fingers together and palm facing down.
Place the hand at the front of your throat.
Make two short downward movements against the throat.
tip: Plural of “Water” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Hold your non-dominant arm in front of you with the wrist facing up.
Tap the top of that wrist twice with your dominant index finger.
tip: Plural of “Time” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Shape both hands into flat open hands, fingers pressed firmly together.
Press the palms together in front of your chest, fingertips pointing forward.
Swing both hands outward and apart twice, like opening a book's covers.
Keep your palms facing each other as the hands open and close.
Mouth the word 'book' silently while you sign, to fix the meaning.
tip: Plural of “Book” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Open your dominant hand with the fingers together, thumb relaxed.
Place the open hand around your chin, fingertips near the jawline.
Slide the hand downward while fingers and thumb close together, tracing a beard.
Keep the palm angled toward your face through the downward slide.
Finish with the hand just below the chin, fingers lightly pinched.
tip: Plural of “Man” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Close your dominant hand, extending only the index finger upward.
Touch the fingertip to your cheek, just below the cheekbone.
Brush the finger downward along the cheek twice, with two light strokes.
Keep the palm facing inward toward your face through both strokes.
Mouth the word 'woman' silently — the same sign also covers girl and lady.
tip: Plural of “Woman” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand relaxed in front of you, palm facing sideways.
Shape your dominant hand with the index finger and thumb pinched together.
Slide the pinched fingers up the ring finger of your non-dominant hand.
Move slowly from the knuckle toward the fingertip, as if fitting a wedding ring.
Smile gently and mouth 'wife', since the same sign also covers husband and spouse.
tip: Plural of “Wife” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Hold both hands as flat blades, fingers together and straight, thumbs tucked.
Rest the flat edge of your dominant hand across the top of the other hand.
Tap the bottom edge of the upper hand against the top edge of the lower hand.
Keep both palms facing sideways, fingertips pointing across your body.
Repeat the small tapping motion twice, keeping your expression businesslike.
tip: “Works” is signed with the base WORK sign.

steps: Hold both hands open and flat in front of your body, fingers together.
Turn both palms to face upward, as if holding two invisible balls.
Circle both hands continuously, the left going one way and the right the other.
Keep the circles small and even, just above waist height.
Smile — play is joyful, and a stiff face reads as mechanical.
tip: “Plays” is signed with the base PLAY sign.

steps: Hold both hands open and flat in front of your body, fingers together.
Turn both palms to face upward, as if holding two invisible balls.
Circle both hands continuously, the left going one way and the right the other.
Keep the circles small and even, just above waist height.
Smile — play is joyful, and a stiff face reads as mechanical.
tip: “Playing” is signed with the base PLAY sign — ASL/BSL marks ongoing action on the sign, not with a separate word.

steps: Hold both hands open and flat in front of your body, fingers together.
Turn both palms to face upward, as if holding two invisible balls.
Circle both hands continuously, the left going one way and the right the other.
Keep the circles small and even, just above waist height.
Smile — play is joyful, and a stiff face reads as mechanical.
tip: Past form of “Play” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Close both hands into tight fists, keeping the thumbs tucked inside.
Hold both fists in front of your chest at shoulder width.
Pump the fists up and down in quick alternation, like pumping arms while running.
Keep the fists vertical, moving about a hand's length with each pump.
Lean your body slightly forward — the lean sells the running motion.
tip: “Runs” is signed with the base RUN sign.

steps: Extend the index and middle fingers of your dominant hand, folding the other fingers away.
Hold the two extended fingers in front of your body, palm facing sideways like scissors blades.
Open and close the two fingers repeatedly in a small, quick snipping motion.
Drift the hand slightly forward as you snip, tracing the line of the cut.
Pair the sign with a neutral expression and mouth 'cut' while you snip.
tip: Plural of “Cut” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Raise both hands into the fingerspelling space in front of your chest.
Fingerspell M, then A, then R with the two-handed BSL alphabet in a smooth flow.
Keep your non-dominant base hand steady while the dominant hand forms each letter.
Mouth 'March' distinctly as the spelling finishes.
tip: Plural of “March” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Raise both hands into the fingerspelling space in front of your chest.
Fingerspell J-U-L-Y with the two-handed BSL alphabet in one fluid run.
Let your dominant hand shape each letter over the steady base hand.
Mouth 'July' clearly as the final Y completes.
tip: Plural of “July” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand flat and open in front of your chest, palm facing your body.
Let the flat hand stand for the ground beneath the growing plant.
Close your dominant hand into a fist behind the flat hand, palm facing you.
Bring the fist round and up in an arc, opening into a flat hand as it rises.
Let the unfurling fingers suggest a flower blooming or a sprout growing.
Mouth 'spring' with a bright, cheerful expression as the hand opens.
tip: Plural of “Spring” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Hold both hands in front of your body with the palms turned toward each other.
Spread your fingers loosely with the hands a few inches apart.
Wiggle all your fingers continuously so they look like flickering flames.
Move the hands alternately up and down in small, quick hops.
Let one hand rise as the other drops, trading places like dancing flames.
Keep a serious expression and mouth 'fire' as the fingers flutter.
tip: Plural of “Fire” — sign the base sign (often repeated) for more than one.

steps: Make a fist with your dominant hand and stick your thumb straight up, holding it in front of your chest.
Hold your other hand in a relaxed fist beside it, about a fist-width away.
Twist your wrist sharply so the thumb flicks from pointing up to pointing across toward your other fist.
Keep your palm facing inward toward the other hand throughout the flick.
tip: “Buying” is signed with the base BUY sign — ASL/BSL marks ongoing action on the sign, not with a separate word.

steps: Make a 'Y' with your dominant hand by extending the thumb and little finger while folding the middle fingers down.
Raise the Y hand to the side of your face, bringing the thumb up beside your mouth with the palm facing you.
Hold the handshape briefly at your cheek, then lower your hand back to a neutral resting position.
tip: “Calling” is signed with the base CALL sign — ASL/BSL marks ongoing action on the sign, not with a separate word.

steps: Extend the index finger of your dominant hand, folding the remaining fingers into a loose fist.
Touch your chin with the fingertip, keeping the finger pointing upward and the palm facing down.
Flick your hand forward away from your chin so the finger points ahead at chest height.
tip: “Saying” is signed with the base SAY sign — ASL/BSL marks ongoing action on the sign, not with a separate word.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand flat in front of you at waist level with the palm facing up.
Curve the fingers of your dominant hand into a rounded cupped shape, as if holding a coin.
Bring the cupped hand down from above and tap your fingertips once onto the open palm.
tip: “Paying” is signed with the base PAY sign — ASL/BSL marks ongoing action on the sign, not with a separate word.

steps: Hold both hands flat with fingers together in front of your chest, palms facing down.
Move your hands toward each other until your dominant hand comes down to rest on top of the other.
Press the stacked hands down slightly, like closing a lid, then hold them together briefly.
tip: “Closing” is signed with the base CLOSE sign — ASL/BSL marks ongoing action on the sign, not with a separate word.

steps: Hold both flat hands in front of your chest with fingers together and palms facing down.
Lift one hand up and place it flat on top of the other, like laying a brick.
Alternate hands, stacking each one on top of the last to build upward layer by layer.
tip: “Building” is signed with the base BUILD sign — ASL/BSL marks ongoing action on the sign, not with a separate word.

steps: Make a firm fist with your dominant hand, wrapping your thumb across your fingers.
Raise the fist to the middle of your chest, holding it a short distance in front of your body.
Turn your wrist so the back of your hand faces forward, with your knuckles pointing away from you.
Hold the fist still in that position for a moment, keeping your other hand relaxed at your side.
tip: “Holding” is signed with the base HOLD sign — ASL/BSL marks ongoing action on the sign, not with a separate word.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand flat in front of your waist, palm facing upward like a small platform.
Form a V with your dominant hand by extending your index and middle fingers, keeping the rest curled.
Point the two V fingers straight down above your upturned palm, with the back of your hand facing forward.
Lower the V fingertips onto your palm so the two fingers stand upright on it, then hold briefly.
tip: “Stands” is signed with the base STAND sign.
